source_text:
In Ruth
ΡΟΥΘ.
12.989 Καὶ ὄνομα τῇ δευτέρᾳ Ῥούθ. Ῥοὺθ τύπον φέρει τῶν ἐθνῶν· ἥτις κατέλιπε τὰ
πάτρια, καὶ ἡνώθη τῇ Ἰσραηλιτικῇ ἕξει. Ζητητέον δὲ πῶς, τοῦ νόμου ἀπαγορεύοντος
μὴ εἰσελθεῖν Μοαβίτην εἰς Ἐκκλησίαν Θεοῦ, ἡ Ῥοὺς Μοαβίτις οὖσα εἰσῆλθε. Καὶ
τοῦτο ζητῶν χρῆσαι τῷ· "∆ικαίω δὲ νόμος οὐ κεῖται, ἀλλὰ ἀδίκοις καὶ
ἀνυποτάκτοις."
pass_a_gloss: And the second was named Ruth. Ruth carries a type of the nations, she who abandoned the ancestral customs and was united to the Israelite way of life. One must investigate how, the law forbidding a Moabite to enter God's Church, Ruth a Moabitess entered. Seeking this, make use of: "Law is not set for a righteous one, but for the unjust and unordered."
pass_b_english: And the name of the second was Ruth. Ruth bears the type of the nations: she left her ancestral ways and was joined to Israel's manner of life.

Yet one must ask how Ruth, a Moabitess, entered when the law forbids a Moabite to enter the assembly of God. Inquiring into this, apply the saying: "[[The law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and rebellious >> Bible:1 Timothy 1:9]]."
